title.en: The Charter of Rights and Freedoms
title.fr: La Charte des droits et libertés

text.en: In 1982, the Constitution of Canada was changed to make the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms a firm part of it.
text.fr: En 1982, la Constitution du Canada a été modifiée pour y inscrire de façon solide la Charte canadienne des droits et libertés.

source.quote: The Constitution of Canada was amended in 1982 to entrench the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms

verification.evidence: The Constitution of Canada was amended in 1982 to entrench the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms

text.en: Canada's Charter of Rights and Freedoms opens with a line that puts the supremacy of God beside the rule of law. Those first words matter in two ways: they say religious traditions have a place in Canadian society, and they say each human being has dignity and worth.
text.fr: La Charte canadienne des droits et libertés s'ouvre sur une phrase qui place la suprématie de Dieu à côté de la primauté du droit. Ces premiers mots comptent de deux façons : ils disent que les traditions religieuses ont leur place dans la société canadienne, et que chaque être humain a une dignité et une valeur.

source.quote: the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, which begins with the words, “Whereas Canada is founded upon principles that recognize the supremacy of God and the rule of law.” This phrase underlines the importance of religious traditions to Canadian society and the dignity and worth of the human person.

verification.evidence: The Constitution of Canada was amended in 1982 to entrench the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, which begins with the words, “Whereas Canada is founded upon principles that recognize the supremacy of God and the rule of law.” This phrase underlines the importance of religious traditions to Canadian society and the dignity and worth of the human person.

text.en: The Charter tries to sum up our fundamental freedoms. It also sets out other rights as well.
text.fr: La Charte tente de résumer nos libertés fondamentales. Elle établit aussi d'autres droits.

source.quote: The Charter attempts to summarize fundamental freedoms while also setting out additional rights.

verification.evidence: The Charter attempts to summarize fundamental freedoms while also setting out additional rights. The most important of these include:

text.en: One of these is mobility rights. Canadians may live and work in any part of Canada they like. They may come into the country and go out of it freely, and they may apply for a passport.
text.fr: L'un d'eux est la liberté de circulation et d'établissement. Les Canadiens peuvent vivre et travailler dans la région du Canada de leur choix. Ils peuvent entrer au pays et en sortir librement, et ils peuvent demander un passeport.

source.quote: Mobility Rights — Canadians can live and work anywhere they choose in Canada, enter and leave the country freely, and apply for a passport.

verification.evidence: The Charter attempts to summarize fundamental freedoms while also setting out additional rights. The most important of these include: • Mobility Rights — Canadians can live and work anywhere they choose in Canada, enter and leave the country freely, and apply for a passport.

text.en: The Charter also protects Aboriginal peoples' rights. The rights it guarantees will not harm any treaty rights, or any other rights or freedoms, that Aboriginal peoples have.
text.fr: La Charte protège aussi les droits des peuples autochtones. Les droits qu'elle garantit ne porteront atteinte à aucun droit issu de traités, ni à aucun autre droit ou liberté des peuples autochtones.

source.quote: Aboriginal Peoples’ Rights — The rights guaranteed in the Charter will not adversely affect any treaty or other rights or freedoms of Aboriginal peoples.

verification.evidence: The Charter attempts to summarize fundamental freedoms while also setting out additional rights. The most important of these include: … • Aboriginal Peoples’ Rights — The rights guaranteed in the Charter will not adversely affect any treaty or other rights or freedoms of Aboriginal peoples.

text.en: It sets out official language rights and minority language education rights. English and French have the same standing in Parliament and across the whole government.
text.fr: Elle établit les droits liés aux langues officielles et les droits à l'instruction dans la langue de la minorité. Le français et l'anglais ont le même statut au Parlement et dans l'ensemble du gouvernement.

source.quote: Official Language Rights and Minority Language Educational Rights — French and English have equal status in Parliament and throughout the government.

verification.evidence: The Charter attempts to summarize fundamental freedoms while also setting out additional rights. The most important of these include: … • Official Language Rights and Minority Language Educational Rights — French and English have equal status in Parliament and throughout the government.

text.en: It names multiculturalism too. Many cultures living together is a basic part of Canada's heritage and identity.
text.fr: Elle nomme aussi le multiculturalisme. La vie commune de nombreuses cultures est un élément fondamental du patrimoine et de l'identité du Canada.

source.quote: Multiculturalism — A fundamental characteristic of the Canadian heritage and identity.

verification.evidence: • Multiculturalism — A fundamental characteristic of the Canadian heritage and identity. Canadians celebrate the gift of one another’s presence and work hard to respect pluralism and live in harmony.

text.en: Canadians see one another's presence as a gift and celebrate it. They work hard to respect pluralism and to live in harmony.
text.fr: Les Canadiens voient la présence des autres comme un cadeau et la célèbrent. Ils travaillent fort pour respecter le pluralisme et vivre en harmonie.

source.quote: Canadians celebrate the gift of one another’s presence and work hard to respect pluralism and live in harmony.

verification.evidence: • Multiculturalism — A fundamental characteristic of the Canadian heritage and identity. Canadians celebrate the gift of one another’s presence and work hard to respect pluralism and live in harmony.
